title: Every one-bit decoration of the pinwheel admits a crystal
claim: Every one of the 1,024 one-bit decorated substitutions of the pinwheel admits a crystal, and so (radius lemma) a periodic plane obeying its law at every radius: one hidden bit per tile, placed by a decorated substitution, never forces the pinwheel. The sixteen decorations ROUND-PRICE-20261108-001's exact census left open are settled by certificates checked with independent code: for 10101 / 00110 and its relabelling 11001 / 01010, 26 periodic parent tilings of 8 to 40 tiles per period, half their tiles turned by arctan(4/3) from the other half, whose cuts obey the law; for the other seven classes, one exported escape each from ONE-BIT-20261108-001B.
failure_conditions: A crystal or certificate is not a tiling, or one of its labelled collars lies outside its decoration's law.
The certificates do not cover exactly the eight classes the exact census left open.
A control fails: the closure counts, the law's independence of its seed, the smallest crystal obeying the law uncut, or a flipped label keeping its cut legal.
foundation_claim_scope: One-bit decorated substitutions of the pinwheel (two labels set through Conway's cut), their labelled collar laws, and periodic planes; exact finite certificates, with the radius lemma for every radius. Other measures of hidden information (edge labels, more labels per tile) are not covered.

validation.independence: check.py imports neither the search (torus_lib, the growth engine) nor the main pipeline (atlas_lib, decor_lib): it rebuilds the collars, their completeness and the labelled law with the knotlab note's standalone replay. Written by Claude in one session at the coordinator's go-ahead on 2026-11-08.
validation.status: certificates checked exactly with controls; no human or external review
validation.novelty: no-overlap-found for the census and the crystals; known methods (decorated substitutions, torus search)
